emergence.summary: An autosomal-recessive disorder of vitamin recycling caused by loss-of-function mutations in BTD, which encodes biotinidase (chr3p25.1) -- the enzyme that liberates free biotin from biocytin (and from small biotinylated peptides) during the normal turnover of the biotin-dependent carboxylases, and that releases protein-bound biotin from dietary protein. When biotinidase fails, biotin is not recycled (and is lost in urine as biocytin), the free-biotin pool falls, and the four biotin-dependent carboxylases (pyruvate carboxylase, propionyl-CoA carboxylase, 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase, acetyl-CoA carboxylase) are progressively under-charged -- a late-onset MULTIPLE CARBOXYLASE DEFICIENCY. Untreated, profound deficiency (<10% residual activity) produces seizures, hypotonia, ataxia, developmental delay, a skin rash and alopecia, sensorineural hearing loss and optic atrophy; partial deficiency (10-30%) is milder. The kit reads this as the free-biotin-availability / carboxylase-throughput axis driven DOWN (an enzyme LOF -> pathway throughput falls, the upstream substrate biocytin accumulates). Correction is, beautifully, the simplest possible REPLACE: oral biotin (vitamin B7) supplies the exact free cofactor the broken recycler would have liberated, FLOODING the free-biotin pool and re-charging the carboxylases -- bypassing the recycling defect entirely. This is one of the most treatable inborn errors of metabolism: identified by newborn screening and treated lifelong with inexpensive oral biotin, pre-symptomatic patients have a normal, symptom-free course. IMPORTANT HONESTY: the corrective DIRECTION (replace the missing cofactor) is forced [F]; the realised MAGNITUDE is [O] and TIMING-limited -- biotin almost completely PREVENTS disease when started before symptoms, but established neurological damage (sensorineural hearing loss, optic atrophy) frequently does NOT reverse once present, and the partial-vs-profound dose is [O]. The BTD coding lesions sit outside the promoter firewall; the gamma read is of the BTD promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr3, gamma 1.3560). Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: free-biotin availability / biotin-dependent carboxylase throughput -- biotinidase recycles biotin from biocytin during carboxylase turnover and releases dietary protein-bound biotin. LOF lowers the free-biotin pool and under-charges the four carboxylases (axis DOWN, multiple carboxylase deficiency). A cofactor-recycling enzyme LOF whose corrective is to flood the missing cofactor

per_gene.note: BTD encodes biotinidase, the hydrolase that liberates free biotin from biocytin and small biotinyl-peptides (recycling biotin from carboxylase turnover) and releases protein-bound biotin from food. LOF -> free biotin is lost as urinary biocytin, the carboxylases are under-charged (late-onset multiple carboxylase deficiency). Profound <10% vs partial 10-30% residual activity. chr3p25.1. autosomal recessive. NCBI official symbol BTD. OMIM 253260.
per_gene.src: Wolf 1983 J Pediatr 103:233 (biotinidase deficiency defined); Cole 1994 J Biol Chem 269:6566 (BTD cloning); Wolf 2010 (GeneReviews, Biotinidase Deficiency)

falsifiers.claim: BTD LOF moves the free-biotin / carboxylase-throughput axis DOWN (the recycler fails, the carboxylases are under-charged)
falsifiers.falsifier: a BTD loss-of-function allele that INCREASED free-biotin availability or carboxylase activity would refute the throughput-down read
falsifiers.measurable_by: plasma free-biotin / urinary biocytin and carboxylase (e.g. propionyl-CoA carboxylase) activity in BTD-deficient patients vs controls

falsifiers.claim: REPLACING biotin is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if oral biotin failed to raise carboxylase activity / failed to prevent the biochemical phenotype in pre-symptomatic biotinidase deficiency, the replace lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: carboxylase activity and clinical / biochemical outcome on oral biotin in newborn-screened biotinidase-deficient infants
